Generate a summary table of numeric variables

Source: R/generate_summary.R
generate_summary.Rd

Generate a summary table of numeric variables

Usage

generate_summary(
  data,
  ...,
  stats = c("n", "mean", "sd", "median", "min", "max"),
  group_as_list = FALSE,
  group_separator = " - ",
  metadata = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame (typically tibble), or a lazy table (e.g. dplyr::tbl() on a database connection), in which case the statistics are computed in the database. Group it with dplyr::group_by() to summarise per group.

...

Numeric variables to summarise (tidyselect). If none are given, every numeric column without value labels is used.

stats

Statistics to compute, any of "n", "n_missing", "mean", "sd", "median", "min", "max", "p25" and "p75". A database that cannot compute one (e.g. SQLite has no quantile() for "p25") gives an error naming it.

group_as_list

Logical. If TRUE, returns a list with one table per group.

group_separator

Character. Separator between group values in list names.

metadata

A named list with optional metadata to attach as attributes, e.g. title, subtitle, and source_note.

Value

A table of class "tsg" with one row per variable (its label in category) and one column per statistic, or a list of such tables when group_as_list = TRUE.

Examples

generate_summary(person_record, age)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   category     n  mean    sd median   min   max
#>   <chr>    <int> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 Age       2918  30.7  21.0     26     0    96

person_record |>
  dplyr::group_by(sex) |>
  generate_summary(age, stats = c("n", "mean", "median"))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   sex        category     n  mean median
#>   <int+lbl>  <chr>    <int> <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 1 [Male]   Age       1516  30.0     25
#> 2 2 [Female] Age       1402  31.5     27
